newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka to allow abortion in limited cases.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka to allow abortion in limited cases.

text.p: Sri Lanka plans to legalise abortion in certain cases, the state-owned Daily News said on Wednesday.

The newspaper said the Indian Ocean island, which now bans all abortions, planned to legalise termination of pregnancy resulting from rape or incest, and in cases where the unborn child was found to be deformed.

The newspaper quoted Wimala de Silva, chairman of the National Committee on Women, as saying the government was also moving towards approving three months' maternity leave for single unmarried mothers.
Maternity leave is now granted only to married mothers.
De Silva said the government was keen to take steps to stop discrimination against children born out of wedlock.
A large number of parents, mostly in rural Sri Lanka, still have children out of wedlock.
Sri Lanka recently created a separate Women's Affairs ministry to handle women issues.
